chunk_findings.detail: If a governed load signal is absent from `load` while other governed signals are present, `_load_step` fails to treat the absent signal as unavailable. For example, with `params.load_thresholds` containing both `"cpu"` and `"mem"`, `last.load=Ladder(level=2, at=0.0)`, `now=400` (cooldown 300), and `load={"cpu": 0.0}` (`"mem"` missing), `seen` is `["cpu"]`, `blind` is `False`, `cand` is `0`, and the function returns `Ladder(0, 400)`. The load ladder drops from level 2 to 0 even though the missing `"mem"` reading could still be high. This violates the requirement that unavailable readings hold the ladder and are never read as zero; `not seen` handles the all-absent case, but partial absence is not marked blind.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/govern.py:_load_step

chunk_findings.detail: `load_thresholds: Mapping[str, Threshold] = field(default_factory=_default_thresholds)` passes `_default_thresholds` as a zero-argument callable. `flowcontrol._default_thresholds` is a mapping of thresholds, not a function, so any `Params()` or `params_from_config(cfg)` that does not explicitly pass `load_thresholds` will call the mapping and raise `TypeError: 'dict' object is not callable` during dataclass construction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/govern.py Params.load_thresholds

chunk_findings.detail: `held` is derived from the global `prev.level >= 1` and is applied to every load signal, but `_load_step` stores no per-signal previous level. With two signals, `cpu` and `memory`, both low=0.5 high=0.8, `last.load = Ladder(level=1, at=0)`, and at `now=400` the load is `{"cpu": 0.1, "memory": 0.6}`: cpu, the signal that caused level 1, is below low, while memory is under high but over low. `_signal_level(0.6, memory, held=True)` returns 1, so `cand == prev.level` and `_load_step` returns the old `Ladder(level=1, ...)` instead of dropping to 0. The only actually high signal has recovered, but a different signal in the hysteresis band falsely keeps the load ladder stuck at level 1.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/govern.py _load_step

chunk_findings.detail: `test_govern_config_defaults_match_params_and_fallbacks_are_strict` calls `Config.load()` and then asserts `g.params_from_config(cfg) == g.Params(...)`. `Config.load()` is environment-sensitive: in any checkout where a user/local ddflow config or environment sets a `[govern]` knob (for example `quota_mark_1 = 0.5`), `params_from_config(cfg)` no longer equals the default `g.Params(...)` and the test fails even when `core/govern.py` is correct. The test should use an isolated default config rather than load the ambient configuration.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_govern.py:164

chunk_findings.detail: The monotonicity property generates the starting `g.Ladder(cl, 0)` with `st.integers(0, 3)`, but the context ladder has five levels: `test_context_ladder` includes `0.95` -> `EMERGENCY`, which corresponds to level 4. The property never starts from an EMERGENCY context state, so a governor that violates monotonicity only when `last.context.level == 4` will pass. This makes the property weaker than its stated guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_govern.py:119
